justification: Follow-up to the DCP-height fallback (#758): live testing on 38 Park Road Bowral showed the fallback read Wingecarribee's DCP height of two storeys as two metres and picked the Heritage-Conservation-Area exception, yielding one storey. That turned the user-facing yield from null into a confident wrong number on a compliance surface, so the height fallback must be unit-aware and reject mis-extractions.

pre_impl.existing_data: Live /api/dcp/structured-controls shows Wingecarribee max_height stored as two rows in STOREYS — a general two-storey control and a one-storey control conditioned on a Heritage Conservation Area — not metres like the LEP height the engine assumed.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The merged #758 fallback used _get_dcp_value which returns a bare float, so it lost the storeys unit and, via prefer_max, chose the smallest cap which was the HCA one-storey exception; the live brief showed effective height one metre and one storey for Bowral.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Adds a small _dcp_height_metres helper reusing the existing _matching_controls; no new data source. Converts storeys to metres via the existing STOREY_HEIGHT_M, prefers unconditioned controls, and rejects a metre height below one storey.

functions.name: _dcp_height_metres
functions.input: the DCP controls list and the development type being assessed for this lot
functions.output: the DCP maximum building height in metres plus a flag for whether the source value was expressed in storeys
functions.if_none: no usable max_height control, or an implausibly small metre value, returns None so the height envelope is skipped rather than computed from a mis-extraction

values.read_at: _dcp_height_metres reads the chosen control's value and unit before the height envelope is computed
values.if_missing: a missing or sub-storey height returns None and the engine records the height as unavailable instead of guessing a storey count

break_it.scenario: A council expresses its DCP maximum height in storeys, as Wingecarribee does with two storeys, rather than in metres
break_it.what_happens: reading the storey count as metres gives a fraction of one storey and a nonsense envelope, the confident-wrong number the live Bowral brief showed
break_it.how: the helper detects the storeys unit and converts to metres via STOREY_HEIGHT_M so the downstream storey calc recovers the correct count
break_it.repro: call _dcp_height_metres with a two-storey control and confirm it returns six metres flagged as storeys, and the engine reports two storeys

break_it.scenario: A council has both a general height and a stricter Heritage-Conservation-Area-only height control for the same development type
break_it.what_happens: picking the smallest cap applies the HCA one-storey limit to an ordinary non-heritage lot and under-reports the envelope
break_it.how: the helper prefers controls with no condition, so the general control applies by default and the conditioned HCA exception is not used blind
break_it.repro: pass a general two-storey and an HCA-conditioned one-storey control and confirm the general two-storey is chosen

break_it.scenario: A DCP height is mis-extracted as a sub-storey value such as Canada Bay's zero point nine metres
break_it.what_happens: computing an envelope from a fence-height-sized value produces a misleading one-storey building limit
break_it.how: a metre value below the one-storey plausibility floor is rejected and the height envelope is left unavailable rather than computed
break_it.repro: call _dcp_height_metres with a zero point nine metre height and confirm it returns None

post_merge.manual_verify: 225 capacity and constraint tests pass including the new TestDcpHeightUnits class; helper simulated live against Wingecarribee's real two rows returning six metres, and against Canada Bay's mistype returning None. Live re-verification on the Bowral brief needs the Railway deploy after merge.
